subject: Aurelia Therapeutics: request for subprocessor roster, access mappings, and SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@aureliamd.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurelia Security Team <security@aureliamd.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: subprocessor roster + SIG clarifications for pilot

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move toward a short pilot, our security team has a few clarifying asks so we can complete the SIG questionnaire and map residual risk for our procurement board. Can you provide the following by EOD Monday if possible?

1) A current subprocessor roster (CSV) that includes: provider name, region of data residency, purpose, and whether they have access to plaintext customer data.
2) An access-mapping document describing which Redwood services/roles touch customer data and the relevant controls (KMS, ephemeral tokens, logging endpoints).
3) Confirmation of any third-party telemetry exports (names and destination domains).

We're attaching the SIG spreadsheet with highlighted rows we care about (column comments are our live questions). If it's easier, a short call to walk through would also be fine.

Best,
Emma Jensen
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Aurelia Therapeutics
Attachment: aurelia-sig-questionnaire-v1.xlsx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@aureliamd.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: subprocessor roster + SIG clarifications for pilot

Emma —

Thanks for the clear asks and the SIG file. We're happy to support the pilot. I'll assemble the roster and an access-mapping summary for the items you flagged. Quick notes:

- I can deliver a CSV roster and a 1-page access matrix by Monday EOD PDT.
- For telemetry exports, I'll verify destinations and include any analytics vendors; we'll mark whether exports contain customer identifiers.
- If you want a walkthrough, I can book a 30-minute slot next Tue (Apr 6).

Looping in Ben Carter (security operations) and Laura Bennett (compliance) to pull the KMS and residency details.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:06:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Aurelia SIG asks — action items

Team —

Aurelia is requesting a subprocessor roster + access mapping and a few clarifications in their SIG. Can you please: 

Ben — collect current KMS ownership mapping (which services use customer KMS keys, ephemeral vs. long-lived keys) and confirm whether any third parties hold encrypted/decrypted keys.
Laura — produce a short residency matrix (region per subprocessor) and confirm which subprocessors qualify as onshore/offshore for contractual purposes.

Target deliverable: CSV roster + one-page access matrix + brief notes on telemetry exports by Monday EOD PDT. If you have partials earlier, send them — I'll combine and send.

Thanks — Connor
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurelia SIG asks — action items

Connor —

Working on it. Quick status:
- KMS mapping: ready for review; most model-serving lanes use customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (we have a handful of internal service accounts that use ephemeral wrapping keys).
- No third parties have access to plaintext keys; a small set of analytics vendors receive hashed telemetry only (list included).

I'll attach the KMS mapping and a short note about key lifecycle.

Ben
Security Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-kms-mapping-20270402.pdf
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@aureliamd.com>
Cc: Aurelia Security Team <security@aureliamd.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Deliverables: subprocessor roster, access matrix, and SIG clarifications

Emma —

Please find the deliverables attached and linked below. Per your highlighted SIG rows, we've added inline answers in the spreadsheet and a short appendix for questions that require contractual language. Summary: 

- Subprocessor roster (attached CSV) — includes provider name, region, purpose, data access level, onshore/offshore designation. (Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-roster-20270401.csv)
- Access matrix (attached PDF + Drive link) — maps Redwood service components to controls (KMS, audit logging endpoints, who can decrypt, retention windows).
- Telemetry exports — list of analytics destinations and whether exported data is pseudonymized; no customer plaintext was included.
- KMS: Ben confirmed customer-managed keys are supported; no external party holds plaintext keys. (Attachment: redwood-kms-mapping-20270402.pdf)

Next steps: If you want a 30-minute walkthrough, I can schedule Tue Apr 6 10:00–10:30 PDT. If the procurement team requires a redline or a DPA addendum for specific subprocessors, please route that to our contracts mailbox and cc me.

Drive folder (artifacts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/67890

Best regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-roster-20270401.csv; redwood-access-matrix-20270405.pdf; redwood-kms-mapping-20270402.pdf
